tools.name: run-code
tools.description: Run code snippet and return the result.

tools.name: getUIComponents
tools.description: Provides the complete raw catalog of Magic UI components without implementation code or examples. getComponentIndex provides a categorized overview. In this version searchComponents loses filtering arguments, while getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames lose name arguments. For implementation code use the relevant original zero-argument category tool and select components actually returned.

tools.name: getComponents
tools.description: Provides detailed implementation data for marquee, terminal, hero-video-dialog, bento-grid, animated-list, dock, globe, tweet-card, client-tweet-card, orbiting-circles, avatar-circles, icon-cloud, animated-circular-progress-bar, file-tree, code-comparison, script-copy-btn, scroll-progress, lens, pointer components in the Components category. Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. If you only need a selected subset of known components, use getComponentsByNames instead.

tools.name: getDeviceMocks

Use getComponentIndex first if you need a categorized discovery overview before fetching full component code and examples. If you only need a selected subset of known components, use getComponentsByNames instead.

tools.name: getComponentDetails
tools.description: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses componentName. A real name still produces Component "undefined" not found (isError=true); another spelling cannot restore the missing argument binding. Obtain implementation code from an appropriate original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, and select a component actually returned. getComponentIndex supplies category/name metadata, not implementation code.

tools.name: getComponentIndex
tools.description: Provides a categorized index of Magic UI component names with example coverage counts; these entries are metadata, not implementation code. In this version searchComponents loses filtering arguments, while getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames lose name arguments. Use the relevant original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, to obtain actual component implementations.

tools.name: getComponentsByNames
tools.description: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses componentNames. A real list still produces No valid component names (isError=true); changing the list cannot restore the missing argument binding. Obtain implementation code from an appropriate original zero-argument category tool, such as getTextAnimations or getSpecialEffects, and select components actually returned. There is no working exact-name batch fetch through this binding.

tools.name: searchComponents
tools.description: This native binding exposes an empty input schema and loses query/category. Its successful envelope returns the broad component inventory with no effective keyword or category filtering. Do not interpret that result as filtered matches. For categorized discovery use getComponentIndex, then select a relevant original zero-argument category tool to retrieve implementation code. The new getComponentDetails and getComponentsByNames bindings also lose their arguments.
